subject: Archive TTL states and delete-ack flow — GreenBank evidence request

Date: 2028-07-02T09:12:00Z
Subject: Archive TTL states — evidence & delete-ack expectations

Hi Hannah,

We're preparing for GreenBank's annual data residency audit and need clarity on how Redwood records deletions for backup/DR copies. Two questions to start: 

1) When customer-side retention TTL expires, what are the distinct states a backup object passes through in Redwood's system (e.g., retained, tombstoned, queued-for-expunge, fully-expunged)? Please give canonical names and typical timing windows.
2) Does Redwood emit a machine-readable "delete-ack" (or equivalent event) once a backup is fully expunged from all replicas in a given region? If so, where is that evidence surfaced (audit log, S3 metadata, API call log, other)?

We're attaching our evidence request template — please fill the fields you can. We need an initial response and an estimated delivery time for a one-page memo + example trace.

Thanks,
Alan Murray
Senior InfoSec Manager
GreenBank

Subject: Re: Archive TTL states — evidence & delete-ack expectations

Alan — thanks for the clear template. Putting a short, high-level answer here and looping in Karthik (storage infra) and Grace (compliance) for details and an ETA.

Quick summary (high level):
- States: retained -> tombstoned -> queued_for_expunge -> expunged.
- Timing: tombstone created immediately after TTL; expunge typically completes within our configured sweep window (default 72 hours) but can be longer for cross-region replication.
- Evidence: we emit expunge events to the audit log and persist an "expunge_ack" event in the customer's audit bucket for Dedicated/Private customers; Hosted customers can request similar traces via support.

Karthik — can you confirm the sweep window numbers, where the ack artifact lives (path + sample), and any caveats (KMS re-encryption windows, cross-region lag)? Grace — I'll need compliance sign-off for the memo.

Next steps: Karthik to provide technical detail + sample trace; we will produce a 1-page memo for GreenBank and an example audit artifact.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt

Subject: Re: Archive TTL states — evidence & delete-ack expectations

Hi all,

Detail below — keeping it pragmatic so GreenBank can map to their audit template.

Canonical object states (internal names / external description):
- retained (internal: state=ACTIVE): backup object is within TTL and available for restore.
- tombstoned (internal: state=MARKED_FOR_DELETE): TTL expired, object marked; visible in object index as tombstone and excluded from standard restores.
- queued_for_expunge (internal: state=EXPUNGE_SCHEDULED): tombstones are batched into expunge waves by region. This is when background workers claim the tombstone for deletion.
- expunged (internal: state=DELETED): object data blocks and metadata are purged; an "expunge_ack" event is emitted and checkpointed to the audit store.

Typical timing windows (default config):
- Tombstone creation: immediate at TTL expiry (0–2 minutes).
- Expunge scheduling: waves every 24 hours by default; our standard Hosted SLO is expunge completion within 72 hours of TTL for same-region copies.
- Cross-region replication: additional lag up to 7 days in worst-case during high load or if replication backlog exists.

Where evidence appears:
- Audit log event: expunge_ack — contains object id, region, timestamp, and expunge_wave_id. Stored in the customer's audit log (audit bucket) for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- For Hosted customers: we maintain internal trace exports; we can provide redacted example traces via support for audit purposes.
- Metadata tags: we write an expunge marker in the object index (not the raw object) — this is internal and surfaced via the audit artifact rather than object-level metadata.

Caveats & edge cases:
- If a backup has been replicated before entry into queued_for_expunge, copies may be expunged asynchronously; expunge_ack is emitted per-region as each region completes. There is no single multi-region aggregated ack today.
- Key destruction: for objects encrypted with customer-managed keys (CMKs/HSM), there is an additional key-revoke procedure which may complicate forensic reconstruction; we include key-rotation and key-destruction markers in the artifact.

Proposed customer-facing deliverables:
- 1-page memo summarizing states + SLOs (deliverable: 2 business days)
- Example expunge trace (redacted) — attached as expunge_trace_example.json (deliverable: 2 business days)
- Optional: set up a webhook or S3 notification for enterprise customers to receive per-region expunge_acks (product request filed: INF-4782).

Attachment: archive_ttl_matrix_v1.xlsx (mapping matrix), expunge_trace_example.json (sample event)

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Staff Engineer, Storage Systems
Redwood Inference

Hannah / Karthik — this is perfect, thanks. A few quick items: 

- The per-region ack behavior is fine; we'll note that in our audit.
- Please attach the one-page memo and the redacted trace to the evidence template and mark the memo as "suitable for auditor consumption."
- Can you confirm whether the expunge_ack event is retained in the audit log for 1 year (GreenBank requirement) or whether we need to request longer retention?

If you can get the memo + trace into the template by end of day Thursday (our time), we can close this request before the audit kickoff next week. If not, a short call on Friday would work.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
